newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip after record-breaking highs.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip after record-breaking highs.

text.p: Egyptian share prices dipped slightly on Thursday at the start of what brokers called a natural correction to weeks of record breaking highs.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said the all-share index fell 0.38 points to 422.71 points in high turnover of 139.86 million pounds ($41.20 million).
"The market is a selling one. Many share prices came down today. It beginning to fall but it's only a natural correction," Rashad Securities Brokerage's Walid el-Khouli told Reuters.
Abu Qir Fertilisiers and Chemicals Industries was the day's most active share, trading in almost 13 million pounds but closed unchanged at 129.73, the CMAsaid.
Brokers have put Abu Qir's strong performance down to its candidacy for a global depositary receipt offering.
The banking sector had another active day, with Misr International Bank/MIBANK leading the way after trading in more than 12.40 million pounds. It closed 42.3 pounds up at 902.
Commercial International Bank (CIB), jumped 42.21 pounds to 886.44 after trade in more than 5.70 million pounds.
"I have a strong feeling this stock will soon hit the 1,000 pounds mark," said Khouli.
National Societe Generale Bank closed 9.5 pounds higher at 1,280 after trading in more than 3.40 million pounds.
Al-Ahram Beverages closed 6.62 pounds higher at 139.02 after trade in more than 1.36 million pounds, with brokers expecting the stock to continue its bull run.
"If this share does not reach 230 pounds I'll go work for a vegetable brokerage," said Khouli.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 736.84 from 732.93 points on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 269.99 from 271.46.
Out of the 92 shares traded, 44 gained, 25 lost and 23 ended the day unchanged.
